text.p: Italy's debt market settled back in directionless trading with operators seeking fresh impetus. The September Bpt contract closed four basis points lower at 137.45 but then turned into positive territory in APT trading.
"The underlying trend is positive but for several days now we've seen profit-taking emerge on upturns and so the market is more or less blocked," one trader said.

The Btp moved in line with wobbly Bunds and then T-Bonds in the afternoon but appeared to shrug off comments by German research body Ifo on Monday saying Italy should be left out of EMU until it proved its fiscal austerity was sustainable.
Traders noted there were some continuing worries the Bundesbank might raise rates to defend the mark but said the dollar's correction today was reassuring.
"It's a market where trading is so thin just a medium-sized order is enough to move prices," one said.
In cash bonds, the February 2007 Btp eased 26 bps to 102.44, yielding 6.50 percent. The Btp/Bund spread widened out to 98 bps while that over Bonos gapped out to 34 bps from a 19 bp low last week.
